scope.method: Scan all358 noteUrdu fields for explicit ہمزہ/ہمزۂ and variant spelling; read all84 matching notes in full and resolve each adjective/possessive/verb antecedent. Scan nonmatching notes for alternate hamza spellings and direct related agreement constructions. This is a focused Urdu agreement audit, not broad stylistic polishing or a new morphology adjudication.

primaryEvidence.title: Qawaid-e-Mir, Tazkir-o-Tanis, letter-name rule
primaryEvidence.finding: The rule explicitly places ہمزہ among masculine letter names. It separately distinguishes the feminine short letter names.
primaryEvidence.application: Use کا for a direct masculine singular hamza head; کے for an oblique head before پر or an oblique plural; رہتا/ہوتا/لکھا/گرتا for a directly coreferential singular predicate.

primaryEvidence.title: Rekhta Dictionary, hamza-e-qatii
primaryEvidence.finding: Dictionary publisher search result labels the technical letter expression اسم، مذکر. The direct page fetch was unavailable, so Qawaid-e-Mir remains the primary adjudicative basis.
